title: High-content assay to measure mitochondrial function and bacterial vacuole size in infected human primary macrophages
protocol: Dilute blood with an equal volume of PBS at room temperature.
Add 15 mL of Lymphocytes Separation Medium to 50 mL Falcon tubes at room temperature.
Pipette slowly 30 mL of PBS-diluted blood over the separation medium, being careful not to mix both phases.
Centrifuge tubes for 30 minutes at room temperature and 300 × g with an acceleration of 2, without breaks.
Retrieve plasma and the PBMC layers (the white band above the Ficoll band).
Transfer to new separate 50 mL tubes.
Add PBS to a final volume of 45 mL.
Centrifuge cells for 10 minutes at 300 × g and 10°C.
Discard supernatant.
Pool all pellets.
Add PBS to a final volume of 45 mL.
Centrifuge cells for 10 minutes at 300 × g and 10°C.
Resuspend the pellet in 2 mL of cold MACS buffer.
Count the cells with Trypan Blue.
Transfer the cells to a 15 mL falcon tube.
Spin down the cells.
Resuspend in 8 μL of MACS buffer for each 1 * 10^6 cells.
Incubate the cells on ice for 5 minutes to prevent internalization of CD14 magnetic beads by phagocytic cells.
Add CD14 magnetic beads to the cells with a volume of 2 μL for each 1 * 10^6 cells.
Incubate at 4°C for 15 minutes with gentle agitation on a roller shaker set at 40 rpm.
Add 5 mL of MACS buffer right after incubation to dilute the beads and avoid non-specific binding.
Centrifuge cells for 10 minutes at 300 × g at 10°C.
Prepare the column and magnet by placing the column on the magnet and the filter on top of the column.
Wash column with 3 mL of MACS buffer.
Remove supernatant after centrifuging.
Resuspend the pellet in 5 μL of MACS buffer for each 1 × 10^6 cells.
Transfer the resuspended cells directly onto the column.
Wait until the last drop before proceeding with three washes of the column using 3 mL of MACS buffer.
Remove the column from the magnet and, at a recommended distance of 30 cm from the magnetic field, add 5 mL of MACS buffer to the column.
Flush the contents with a plunger into a 15 mL tube.

Add cells to a new column without filter and repeat steps resuspending, transferring onto the column, waiting until the last drop, washing the column, removing the column from the magnet, adding buffer, and flushing contents.
Count cells after processing.
Centrifuge cells for 10 minutes at 300 × g at 10°C.
Discard supernatant after centrifuging.
Prepare medium for differentiation using X-VIVO-15 or RPMI supplemented with 25 ng/mL of rh-MCSF and warm it up to 37°C.
Plate cells in 10 cm Nunc™ UpCell™ dishes if the cell count is 8 × 10^6 in 12 mL, or in 6-well Nunc™ UpCell™ plates if the cell count is 1 × 10^6 per well in 2 mL.
Keep cells in a humidified incubator at 37°C + 5% CO2.
Add 6 mL of pre-warmed rh-MCSF supplemented culture medium to a 10 cm dish.
Wait until day 6-7 after plating to obtain fully differentiated macrophages.
Place plates at 20°C for 20 min inside an incubator or at RT on a bench-top for the cells to detach.
Collect half of the supernatant and place it in a 15 mL Falcon tube.
Flush the dish or well with remaining medium to further detach cells and collect them in the falcon tube.
Add 5 mL and 1 mL of PBS to the dish and well, respectively, and repeat the flushing step.
Check with the microscope for good detachment of cells.
Repeat the detachment steps if necessary.
Spin down harvested cells at 400 × g for 10 min at RT.
Resuspend cells in preferred culture medium without phenol red and count cells.
Pause point: Continue the experiment or freeze hMDMs in CryoStor® CS10 freezing medium or in 1 mL of 10% DMSO in FCS at a concentration between 0.5 to 10 * 10^6 cells/mL.
Differentiated hMDMs can be conserved in liquid nitrogen for several months.
Streak L. pneumophila strains from the -80°C glycerol stock on Charcoal Yeast Extract (BCYE) agar.
Incubate the plate for 3 days at 37°C.
Inoculate 10 mL Buffered Yeast Extract (BYE) liquid medium with bacteria at an OD600 of 0.1.
Allow bacteria to grow overnight while shaking at 37°C at 200 rpm.
Grow until OD600 reaches approximately 4.2.
Monitor the bacteria under the light microscope to check they are motile.
Aliquot 2 mL of the bacterial culture.
Measure OD600 of the aliquoted bacterial culture.
Use an OD600 = 2.5 to calculate a concentration of 2.2 × 10^9 bacteria/mL.
Dilute the bacteria in final cell culture medium to obtain a multiplicity of infection (MOI) of 10.
Adjust the concentration of hMDMs to 200,000 cells/mL using culture media.
Add 50 μL per well into a 384-well plate to achieve a final concentration of about 10,000 cells per well.
Leave the cells to attach overnight in the 384-well plate.
Wash hMDMs twice by removing 40 μL of medium.
Gently flush attached hMDMs with 40 μL of fresh phenol red-free culture medium.
Keep the final volume in each well at 50 μL.
Remove 25 μL from all wells.
Add 25 μL of a 2× bacterial suspension to wells meant for infection.
Add culture media to the other wells.
Spin the plate at 200 g for 5 min at room temperature to synchronize infection.
Consider this time as T = 0 of the infection.
Incubate the plate at 37°C for 5 min in a water bath.
Incubate the plate at 37°C + 5% CO2 in a humidified incubator for 25 min.
Wash cells three times to remove extracellular bacteria.
Proceed with staining.
Prepare the 2× dye mix to a final concentration of 200 ng/mL of Hoechst H33342, 10 nM of TMRM, and 1/100 Annexin-V-Alexa Fluor 647 in prewarmed phenol red-free culture medium.
Remove 25 μL of culture medium from cells.
Add 25 μL of the 2× dye mix to cells.
Incubate cells for 30 min at 37°C / 5% CO2 (1 h post infection).
Proceed with image acquisition.
Stabilize the incubation chamber of the microscope at 37°C / 5% CO2.
Load the 384-well plate onto the microscope system.
Adjust the focus for each channel.
Set up exposure time and laser intensity for each channel.
Program the acquisition to image multiple fields per well every hour.
Start acquisition at least 30 minutes after staining.
Prepare automatic high-content image analysis.
Use Perkin Elmer’s High-Content Imaging and Analysis software Harmony® for analysis.
Write a script using pre-programmed blocks from the software.
Segment cellular and subcellular parameters using the fluorescent signal of the staining.
Calculate a mask of nuclei from the input image using the Hoechst signal in the 405/450 channel.
Create a new channel called “calculated image nuclei” based on the nuclei mask.
Find and identify nuclei using the “calculated image nuclei” channel.
Calculate morphological properties of identified nuclei to filter out objects that were wrongly selected.
Use nuclei roundness and area to eliminate artefacts from the analysis.
Check several timepoints when filtering out objects to avoid being too strict.
Create a mask for the cellular cytoplasm by summing up TMRM and Annexin V signals in the 561/600 and 640/690 channels.
Test different detection methods provided by the software as ready-to-use processing modules.
Detect the cytoplasm region among the “real nuclei” population created in the previous step using the mask of cellular cytoplasm.
Resize the regions selected as cytoplasm to 30% to completely encompass each cell.
Measure the intensity in the 561/600 channel for TMRM (mean and SD).
Calculate SD/Mean for TMRM.
Measure the intensity in the 640/690 channel for Annexin V (mean).
Identify infected cells.
Detect bacteria within the “real nuclei” population using the GFP signal in the 488/540 channel.
Calculate morphological properties such as area in μm² to follow the evolution of the vacuole size over time.
Discriminate infected cells from non-infected cells.
Select the desired calculated outputs depending on the experiment e.g., total number of cells ("real nuclei").
Note the number of infected cells.
Determine the number of spots per cell (bacteria).
Calculate the sum of spot area in μm² per cell.
Measure the intensity of TMRM per cell (mean, SD and SD/mean).
Measure the intensity of Annexin-V per cell (mean).
